properties.name: When two linked designs disagree at a seam, say so
properties.statement:
NOW ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN ARGUMENT (trial against dynograph-foundation, 2026-07-28). The open question was whether `compose_and_analyse` plus the ordinary detectors is enough, or whether a dedicated incompatibility check is needed. It is not enough, and the trial shows exactly where the line falls.

WHAT WAS RUN. dynograph-foundation published its offer (`docs/published-surface.json`, 15 boundaries: 11 library, 3 REST, 1 data). reflow2 composed against it in a throwaway graph seeded from its own committed export. Their 31 nodes and 61 edges imported with ZERO skipped edges.

ROUND ONE, before any matching: 0 seam findings, and one loud structural signal — "29 nodes form a cluster disconnected from the rest of the design". That is the detector correctly reporting that two designs were placed side by side and nothing joined them. Useful, and exactly right.

ROUND TWO, after drawing seven CONSUMES edges by hand from reflow2's components to their published boundaries (store→storage-api and core-api, schema→schema-doc, search→text-api, ingest→resolution-api, heal→graph-api, dimensions→vector-api): the disconnected-cluster finding DISAPPEARED, and the seam produced **zero findings of any kind**. What remained were two findings wholly inside the provider's design.

WHAT THAT PROVES. Composition plus the ordinary detectors checks CONNECTIVITY, not COMPATIBILITY. The existing detectors reason about structure — missing intent, unsatisfied requirements, orphans, cycles, single points of failure — and a well-formed seam trips none of them. But a contract mismatch is a comparison of PROPERTIES ACROSS A PAIR of interfaces: my expected payload format against theirs, my required auth against theirs, my assumed paradigm against theirs, a behavioural promise against its absence. No ordinary detector compares two nodes' properties against each other, so no ordinary detector can ever produce that finding. The silence was not the absence of problems; it was the absence of anyone looking.

THE SECOND HALF, and it is worse. The seven seam edges were HAND-ASSERTED and nothing checked them. I claimed `cmp:store` consumes `dynograph::ifc:storage-api` and the graph accepted it without question. A WRONG hand-match produces exactly the same clean result as a right one — so today the seam analysis is only as good as the assertion nobody verified. That is `req:complementary-pairing`'s job on the matching side, and this requirement's job on the terms side.

WHAT IT MUST CHECK, from the properties `req:interface-spec-complete` already put on Interface: `paradigm` (a consumer written for request-response cannot be pointed at an event feed), `payload_format` (protobuf against JSON fails immediately and totally), `auth` and `transport_security` (the consumer that assumed `none` gets 401s in production; a provider offering `none` against a consumer requiring `tls` is a refusal to connect), `operations` (calling an operation the provider does not offer), `error_model`, and `payload_schema`. Plus the behavioural terms that `req:publishable-promise` would let a surface carry at all.

REPORT, DO NOT JUDGE. A mismatch is a finding to put to the two sides, not a verdict — `unspecified` on either side is an unknown, not a conflict, and must read as "nobody has said" rather than as agreement. The false-green rule from the trial applies here too: silence must never be reported as compatibility.
